PASS: QA1 gate 1, round 1: PASS. Audited commit 3568b56 against the current sprint file. I re-read it fresh; it is unchanged since commit 84c5fb2, and no criterion asserts anything between versions.

R1 Met. Migration 20261122142918_reading_date_navigation.sql:
- Both functions are security definer, language sql, stable, with set search_path = public, and both filter horoscope is not null.
- Return types are declared column by column. get_adjacent_reading_dates returns table (previous_date date, next_date date). get_recent_reading_dates returns table (event_date date). No setof readings and no other column.
- R1a uses strict < and > inside max/min subqueries, so it returns exactly one row with null sides.
- R1b uses group by event_date, order by max(horoscope_generated_at) desc nulls last, event_date desc, then limit 20. The function takes no parameter, so nothing can raise the cap.
- Grants: execute is revoked from PUBLIC and service_role and granted to anon and authenticated only. That is stricter than get_reading_by_date, which only grants, and it is safe because the page reads as anon.
- There is no new policy, and the file ends with the schema_migrations insert.

R2 and R3 Met. DateNavigation.tsx:
- Links use datePagePath, so they go to /date/YYYY-MM-DD, labelled with formatLongDate as "D Month YYYY".
- An absent side renders nothing.
- The current date renders as a span with aria-current="page", not a link.
- When there are no dates at all, the component returns null.

R4 Met.
- loadDateNavigation classifies both RPCs with isDatabaseUnavailable("dateLookup"), which excepts no code. That is correct because the date is pre-validated.
- Each failure is logged in full under its own label.
- If either lookup fails, the result is kind "unavailable", and the component renders null with no notice of its own.
- Traced the double-failure case: page.tsx renders SavedHoroscopesUnavailable once, from page.saved, and the navigation adds nothing.
- The lookup runs in Promise.all beside loadDatePage, not inside it. supabase-js returns errors and does not reject, so the chart and events can't be blanked by it.

R5 Met. The GET path has two .rpc reads on the anon client only. There is no insert, no set_reading_horoscope, no admin client and no OpenAI client. connection() is still in place, and there is no revalidate or force-static under app/date. The build lists /date/[date] as dynamic.

R6 Met statically. The navigation renders inside belowDateBand, right under DatePicker. It is all flex-wrap with min-width 0 and no fixed widths. On mobile, the list sits behind a native details element, and visibility uses reading.module.css desktopOnly/mobileOnly, which exist. Every CSS token used is defined in globals.css. Real 390px layout is LiveQA's step 7.

R7 Met. git diff 3568b56~1 3568b56 -- app/reading app/chart is empty. availability.ts changed in its doc comment only.

R8 Met as written.
- The RLS suite covers every listed R1a and R1b case, the shape of both results, the no-limit-argument case, and the anon select and insert denial.
- The unit suite covers no previous or next, the current date in the list, an empty list, and adjacent, recent and both unavailable, logged in full.
- vitest.rls.config.ts sets fileParallelism false so the order assertions hold.
- I ran these myself:
  - npm test: 25 files, 260 tests, green.
  - typecheck: clean.
  - lint: clean.
  - build: clean.
- I could NOT run test:rls: there is no docker in this WSL distro. The RLS suite's first real run is CI's rls-tests job, so Pipeman's push report must show it green, as the sprint file says.

Low, non-blocking:
(a) The adjacency clusters pick a random base in 3000-3900. On a persistent local database that accumulates runs, two clusters within about 17 days of each other would collide and flake. That is negligible on CI's fresh database.
(b) The recent list is in the DOM twice, once per breakpoint, the same pattern ReadingView already uses. The hidden copy is display:none, so it is out of the accessibility tree.

No Human Prerequisites beyond the sprint file's own: Supabase must be awake for migrate and for LiveQA.

The working tree has an uncommitted CLAUDE.md change: the Next.js agent-rules block that next build re-adds. It is not part of 3568b56 and not audited.

No test was labelled known-failing.
commit=3568b56 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 3568b56f31720936d66db016c836aef3dfda0cec all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Tested on 2026-11-22 against https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app.
Shipped commit 3568b56. Production serves the pushed bookkeeping tip 6c1f89b: /api/health/db
reports status ok, migrationVersion 20261122142918_reading_date_navigation, commit 6c1f89b.
git diff --stat 3568b56 6c1f89b touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-29.json.
Tools: headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57, real link clicks), curl, gh run view --log.

CI: runs 45034516835 (3568b56) and 45034972492 (6c1f89b). build, rls-tests and migrate all
succeed in both. Unit tests 260 passed (25 files). The RLS suite passed 30/30, including
reading-date-navigation.test.ts with 13 tests. migrate applied 20261122142918 in the first run
and printed "Remote database is up to date." in the second. "No drift detected." in both.

STEP 1, seeding: not needed. Production already had 32 dates with a horoscope. That is more
than the 20 cap, so the cap is exercised by real data.

STEP 2, prev/next: PASS. I followed the links with real clicks from /date/2026-11-22 back to
the start and forward to the end. The chain covers 32 dates (all with a horoscope) and is consistent both ways: each
page's next is the page it was reached from. Every page I landed on shows "The reading /
WRITTEN" with its saved text. A middle example: /date/2026-11-19 shows prev 16 November 2026
(/date/2026-11-16) and next 16 December 2026 (/date/2026-12-16).

STEP 3, edges: PASS. /date/1776-07-04 has prev null and shows only "NEXT READING -> 1 January
1900". /date/2100-12-31 has next null and shows only "PREVIOUS READING". Neither page has a
placeholder, aria-disabled element or disabled button (checked in the DOM and on screenshots).

STEP 4, recent list: PASS. There are exactly 20 entries, labelled in long-date format (for
example "16 December 2026"), each linking to /date/YYYY-MM-DD. On its own page the current
date renders as a SPAN with aria-current="page", not a link. This held for 29 February 1984,
16 December 2026 and 4 July 1776. Every entry is a page in the step-2 walk, and each returned
200 with a written horoscope.
Limit: the site never shows when a horoscope was written, so ordering past the top entry can't
be checked from the UI. Step 5 shows that the newest one goes first.

STEP 5, freshness: PASS. I cast one LiveQA seeding horoscope on 2050-06-15 through the date
page's "Write the horoscope" button, at about 15:00:51Z. It went WRITING and then WRITTEN, and
the saved text begins "On June 15, 2050, Venus was in conjunction with Jupiter." That is a
permanent production row, recorded here so it isn't mistaken for organic use. Before the cast,
16 December 2026's next link was 31 December 2100 and the top of the recent list was 19
November 2026.
After reloading OTHER pages:
- /date/1984-02-29: the recent list starts "15 June 2050, 19 November 2026, ...", still 20
  entries, and 8 May 1945 has dropped off.
- /date/2026-12-16: next is now "15 June 2050".
- /date/2100-12-31: previous is now "15 June 2050".

STEP 6, dates only: PASS. Called directly with the anon/publishable key against
rzlojpwlhbcfzpohbwso.supabase.co.
- The key is NOT in any deployed client bundle. I fetched every _next/static chunk for the
  date page and /chart and found no supabase URL, eyJ token or sb_publishable_ key. The step
  says "from the deployed bundle", but the app only uses the key server-side. The user
  supplied the publishable key from the dashboard.
- rpc get_adjacent_reading_dates {"reading_date":"2026-12-16"} returned HTTP 200
  [{"previous_date":"2026-11-19","next_date":"2050-06-15"}].
- Called for 1776-07-04 it returned [{"previous_date":null,"next_date":"1900-01-01"}]. For
  2100-12-31 it returned [{"previous_date":"2050-06-15","next_date":null}].
- rpc get_recent_reading_dates {} returned HTTP 200: 20 objects, each only {"event_date":...},
  starting 2050-06-15 and ending 1776-07-04. This is the same order the page shows.
- get_recent_reading_dates with {"limit":100} returned HTTP 404 PGRST202 "Could not find the
  function public.get_recent_reading_dates(limit)". No argument can raise the cap.
- Direct anon GET /rest/v1/readings?select=* returned HTTP 200 []. select=horoscope also
  returned []. RLS exposes no rows, even though 33 dates with horoscopes exist after the cast.
- No horoscope text, id or events appear in any response. I did not attempt an anon insert
  against production, because the step doesn't require it and a success would write a row.
  The insert denial is covered by CI's RLS suite.

STEP 7, 390px: PASS. I used isMobile at 390x844 on /date/2026-12-16, /date/1776-07-04,
/date/2100-12-31 and /date/2026-11-22. scrollWidth is 390 both with the "RECENTLY WRITTEN (20)"
disclosure closed and with it open. With it open there are 20 items and no element extends
past 390px. Prev and next sit side by side under the date picker.

STEP 8, other routes: PASS. / returns 307 to /date/2026-11-22. /chart and
/chart?date=1969-07-20 return 200. /reading/047e8dbd-385c-4ce0-adc3-acbf7bd9856d returns 200
and renders its 3-step page as before. /reading/abc returns 404. Neither /chart nor /reading
contains "Previous reading", "Next reading", "Recently written" or "Dates with readings".

No console errors or page errors on the date pages.
